Renamed both to `"SUSI_SOLVE"` so the check is finally live. (2) **Dead `trust_level` config**: `config.default.json`'s `trust_level` ("Balanced") had an accessor (`SusiConfig::trust_level`) with zero callers anywhere in the swarm/peer/tool dispatch logic — confirmed dead via the type alias's own comment in `sandbox/manager.rs` (`"conservative", "balanced", "autonomous", "any_new_level"`), which documented an intent nothing implemented. Wired it into Neural Agent Synthesis (`GawdAgentFleet::synthesize_fleet`, Mandate 16's "structural synthesis" of a brand-new specialist agent via LLM): added `GawdAgentFleet::synthesis_similarity_threshold(trust_level)` (0.7 conservative / 0.4 balanced-and-default / 0.2 autonomous) in place of the hardcoded `0.4` similarity-gap threshold that used to fire regardless of configured trust. (3) **Missing peer-federation auth**: `SusiSupervisor::dispatch_peer_task` (`src/gawd/amas.rs`) — used by swarm consensus broadcast, cluster sync, checkpoint replication, and reflex-learning broadcast — never attached an `Authorization` header, so the moment an operator sets `api_auth_token` on any node beyond localhost (exactly what Mandate 40 expects), every peer-to-peer federation call across their own fleet starts silently 401ing. entries.milestone: Directed non-inference performance sweep: every CLI invocation was paying a ~120ms SHA-256 tax on its own 120MB binary
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-19: user directed "make susi lightning fast" outside the model-inference path itself (which is hardware/model-bound and out of scope by their own framing). Audited the CLI invocation path (`main.rs` -> `ensure_daemon_running`) rather than the inference hot loop. Config/messages loading (`SusiConfig::load`, `SusiMessages::load_global`) already had mtime-gated in-process caches; swarm dispatch (`dispatch_explosive_swarm`, `amas.rs`) was already `rayon`-parallel with governance-first sequencing; `check_status`'s lock-file check was already cheap (stat + small read + `kill(pid,0)`). One real, measured bottleneck found: `ensure_daemon_running`'s common-case path (daemon already running, the steady state after first start) called `verify_binary_integrity(current_exe, ...)` unconditionally before returning — and `current_exe` resolves to the `susi-engine` binary itself, not the small `susi` launcher that spawns it. `verify_binary_integrity` re-read and SHA-256-hashed the entire binary from disk on every single invocation with no caching at all. Measured live on this host's real installed `~/.susi/bin/susi-engine` (120MB): **120.8ms** per hash — meaning every ordinary command paid this cost just to reach the "nothing changed, proceed" branch, ~60,000x over Mandate 4's 2ms client-reflex budget, on top of the process-spawn cost the `susi` launcher already pays forwarding to `susi-engine`. Root cause: no caching existed at all, not a cache with a wrong invalidation key (IDENTITY.md's own doc comment on this function already warns against a specific *prior* attempt — a `len:mtime` shortcut that replaced the hash value's format itself and diverged from `susi admin sync`'s SHA-256 writer, causing spurious mismatches). Fixed without repeating that mistake: added `calculate_binary_hash_cached`, a small mtime(nanosecond)+size-gated sidecar cache (`binary.hash.cache`, separate file from `binary.hash` itself) that skips re-reading/re-hashing when the binary provably hasn't changed since the last time *this exact function* hashed it, and falls back to a real, fresh SHA-256 on any cache miss or mismatch — `current_sig`'s actual value and format are byte-identical to before in every case, only the redundant re-computation is skipped, so `binary.hash`'s existing contract with `susi admin sync` (the writer) and `is_trusted_susi_process` (a separate, deliberately-untouched security check, not on this hot per-invocation path) is unaffected. Measured post-fix, same real binary: **120.5ms** on the first (cache-populating) call, **13.4µs** on every call after — a ~9,000x reduction for the steady-state case that dominates real-world usage. New test (`daemon::server::tests::test_binary_hash_cache_hits_on_unchanged_file_and_misses_after_real_change`) proves the cache is actually consulted (not just correct) by planting a wrong sentinel hash directly into the sidecar and confirming an unchanged file serves it, then confirms a genuine content change invalidates it. Not done in this pass: the `susi` launcher's own per-invocation process-spawn (`Command::new(engine_path).status()`, forwarding every call to a fresh `susi-engine` child process) is a separate, architectural cost not addressed here; the live `global susi` daemon on this host was left running and was not restarted, since it was actively serving a real workspace (`~/Downloads`) at audit time — this fix takes effect on the next natural daemon/CLI restart, not retroactively on the already-running process. 166/166 `cargo test --lib` passing (up from 165), `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under default and `--features cuda`.

entries.milestone: Directed follow-up: fix the `susi` launcher itself (`src/native/susi`)
entries.proof: FIXED 2026-09-19: user directed fixing the launcher specifically, following EV-2022920-040's note that its per-invocation process-spawn was flagged but not addressed. Measured first to separate real cost from assumption: direct `susi-engine` invocation vs. via the `susi` launcher (fork+exec+wait) were statistically indistinguishable (~58-64ms either way on this host's real installed binaries) — the launcher's own fork+wait overhead is genuinely small against a large binary's own startup cost, not the dominant factor. Found a real correctness bug instead while reading the 36-line launcher end to end: neither branch of the old `Command::new(...).status()` call ever inspected the resulting `Ok(status)` - `fn main()` simply fell off the end after both success and failure, so the launcher unconditionally exited 0 regardless of what `susi-engine` actually returned. Concretely, any real error from the engine (bad flags, a governance block, an inference failure) was invisible to `&&`, `$?`, or any CI pipeline checking the exit code - the launcher always reported success. Fixed two things together: (1) the exit-code bug, and (2) on Unix, replaced the fork+wait with `std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::exec()`, which replaces the launcher's own process image with `susi-engine`'s - the real exit code reaches the caller directly with no forwarding logic needed at all (a whole class of "did I remember to propagate this" bugs made structurally impossible rather than just fixed once), and removes the redundant fork. Windows has no POSIX `exec`, so that path keeps `status()` but now explicitly calls `std::process::exit(status.code().unwrap_or(1))`. Verified live end-to-end against a real fake `susi-engine` binary (not the real one, to get a deterministic, fast, controlled exit code): unchanged code before the fix always returned 0 to the shell even when the fake engine exited 7; after the fix, `$?` correctly reports 7, and stdout/exit-0 behavior for a genuine success case was also confirmed unchanged. Also fixed a pre-existing `clippy::ptr_arg` warning (`&PathBuf` where `&Path` suffices) found while touching this file - this sub-crate (`src/native/susi`, not a workspace member of the root `Cargo.toml`, built and versioned independently) had never been clippy-gated as part of any prior release check in this ledger. Not fixed: the fallback-to-PATH search when `~/.susi/bin/susi-engine` isn't provisioned yet is unchanged and untested end-to-end here (exercising it cleanly requires removing `susi-engine` from `PATH` too, not just overriding `HOME`, which the live verification above didn't need). `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean for this sub-crate; `cargo build --release` succeeds (358KB binary, opt-level "z" + LTO + strip, unchanged from before).

entries.milestone: Directed follow-up: dug into why a `systemctl restart` of the live daemon didn't shut down cleanly

Verified this directly: sending `SIGTERM` to two live daemon processes made them exit cleanly within the expected window. The actual live host showed something different and far more concerning while investigating: the legitimate daemon (workspace `~/Downloads`) was being `SIGKILL`'d roughly every 60-90 seconds, restart counter climbing, **without me sending it any signal at all**. Root-caused via `ps aux`: my own earlier launcher-testing commands (`./target/release/susi ...` invoked from `src/native/susi/` during EV-2022920-041's verification) had each spawned a **second and third full daemon instance** - `ps` showed three concurrent `susi-engine daemon-start` processes for three different `--workspace` values, backed by three different `substrate_<hash>.lock` files. `GEMI`/`GMCP`/`UDP` (Mandate 31: "central... network ports") bind to `0.0.0.0` - genuinely global, shared resources - but `run_daemon_loop` (since EV-2022920-026's per-workspace lock split) only ever acquired and wrote its PID to the *workspace-scoped* lock file, never the global `substrate.lock` fallback `check_status` was supposed to consult across workspaces. Confirmed via `ls`: `substrate.lock` was 0 bytes, stale since install day - nothing had written to it since the per-workspace split, silently defeating its own cross-workspace detection purpose. Net effect: a `susi` invocation from *any* directory other than the daemon's own workspace found no lock, no signal, no already-running belief, and happily started a competing daemon; the newcomer's port-bind collision triggered its own "Sovereign Eviction" self-healing reflex (`attempt_port_reclaim`, Mandate 22), which correctly identifies the trusted binary holding the port and `SIGKILL`s it outright - explaining the specific `status=9/KILL` signature (not a timeout; an active, deliberate, working-as-designed kill aimed at the wrong target) and its ~60-90s periodicity (however often a stray CLI call landed). Fixed at the actual mutual-exclusion layer, not by patching the symptom: `run_daemon_loop` now also acquires (`flock`, matching the existing workspace lock's mechanism) and writes its PID to the global lock file before binding any port; a daemon for a second workspace that can't acquire it refuses to start instead of racing for the ports. `DaemonContext` now holds both locks (`_lock`, `_global_lock`), released together on shutdown; `stop_daemon` now removes both lock files instead of only whichever one it happened to pick, so a stale PID can't linger in the other for a future `check_status` to trip over. New test `test_global_lock_is_mutually_exclusive_across_different_workspace_paths` proves the actual property (second acquire fails while the first holds it, succeeds once released) rather than just exercising the code path. Verified live: killed the two rogue instances, cleaned their stale lock files, and the legitimate daemon has now run continuously with zero further kills (10+ minutes and counting at time of writing, versus the prior ~60-90s cadence). 167/167 `cargo test --lib` passing (up from 166), `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean under default and `--features cuda`.

entries.milestone: EV-2022920-042's own global-lock fix exposed a second, related bug: binary-change restarts targeted the wrong workspace

Root cause: `routing.rs`'s `load_preference`/`save_preference` resolve through `susi_paths::SusiDirs::config_dir()`, which reads the process-global `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` env vars; `routing.rs`'s own `cloud_failover_order_prefers_sticky_vendor_once` test temporarily redirects those same env vars under a local `ENV_LOCK`, and `http_provider.rs` (same crate, same test binary) independently redirects them too under its own separate `cloud_env_test_lock()` — neither lock knew about the other, and `preferred_cloud_substring_match` didn't hold either one, so a concurrent env redirect from any of those tests could make it read/write the wrong config dir mid-test. Fixed by adding one shared `crate::engines::env_test_lock()` (crates/susi-gemi/src/engines/mod.rs) and switching all three call sites (both `routing.rs` tests, both `http_provider.rs` tests) onto it, deleting the two now-redundant private locks. Verified: `cargo test -p susi-gemi --lib` run 8 times back-to-back under default parallelism, 63/63 passed each time (previously observed to fail intermittently); `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` both clean afterward.

RSI iteration 1/100: automatic reflex distillation now fails closed. The audit previously treated unreadable staged data and global-config errors as empty/default state, returned training failures inside an Ok string, and ignored failure to delete consumed samples. It now distinguishes absent staging from unreadable staging, propagates configuration and training errors as typed EaiError values, and surfaces sample-retirement failure. Regression tests cover absent, populated including unterminated-final-line, and unreadable staging. Targeted fmt, test, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 2/100: native reflex training is now cumulative and single-writer. The prior implementation initialized a fresh random VarMap for every run, trained it, and replaced the previous weights, so repeated distillation did not improve the existing model. It now acquires a cross-process reflex-training lock, resolves configuration without a silent default, creates the model directory explicitly, loads published weights into the trainable variables when present, then atomically renames the trained checkpoint. Existing but unreadable/incompatible weights abort training instead of being silently discarded. The result text now accurately says native cumulative training rather than autonomous evolution. Targeted fmt, test, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

ProtocolKnowledgeBase stages pairs at <workspace>/.susi/distillation_staged.jsonl, but ReflexTrainer ignored its workspace argument and looked only in the host config directory; therefore normal workspace experience could never trigger or feed training. SusiAlphaModel now separates the globally published model directory from an explicit staged-data path, while the existing global-buffer entry point remains as a compatibility wrapper. ReflexTrainer uses the invoking workspace buffer for thresholding, training, and post-success retirement, while retaining the globally shared weights and cross-process training lock. Regression tests prove malformed records retain line attribution, substring guesses are rejected, and canonical case-insensitive actions map to the correct label. Unknown schema, malformed sidecar, invalid labels, or weight mismatch fails closed. A regression test writes a valid pair, proves it loads, mutates only the weights, and proves mismatch rejection. RSI iteration 10/100: reflex checkpoint publication is now crash-safe as a bundle. Readers resolve only the manifest's same-directory filename and reject traversal, unsupported schema, missing checkpoint, corrupt vocabulary, or digest mismatch; a crash before the manifest update leaves the prior generation active. Legacy configured weight files remain readable and migrate on the next successful training publication. Cache fingerprinting follows the manifest rather than a legacy filename. Regression coverage proves valid local resolution and traversal rejection. Generation retention cleanup remains a later lifecycle iteration; correctness no longer depends on it. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 11/100: reflex bundles now retain and recover from one last-known-good generation. Each publication records the previously validated checkpoint in the atomic manifest. Inference validates active vocabulary/hash/safetensors construction first and automatically tries previous on any active failure; cumulative training selects the first hash-valid active-or-previous source instead of becoming permanently wedged by a damaged active file. Both manifest paths are constrained to local filenames. A regression test creates a corrupt active generation and valid hash-bound previous generation and proves usable_checkpoint selects the previous mapping. This converts iteration 9's detection and iteration 10's crash-safe pointer into an operational recovery path. Retention cleanup of generations older than active+previous remains the next lifecycle concern. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 12/100: immutable reflex checkpoint generations now have bounded lifecycle retention. After the new manifest is durably published, SUSI preserves exactly the active and last-known-good checkpoint pairs and removes only generation files matching its strict <stem>.<u128-generation>.<u32-pid>.safetensors naming scheme plus their vocabulary sidecars; legacy configured weights and unrelated similarly named files are not candidates. Cleanup runs only after pointer publication, so failure cannot invalidate the active bundle, and any removal failures are surfaced in the successful training report as cleanup warnings rather than falsely turning a completed model publication into a failed training transaction. Regression coverage proves active/previous and unrelated files survive while an older generated pair is removed. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 13/100: reflex training no longer loses receipts captured during a training run. The trainer previously read the live workspace JSONL and deleted that same path after training, racing receipt capture; any append between read and delete vanished unlearned. Automatic and forced training now acquire the producer's cross-process staging lock, atomically rename the eligible buffer into a unique claim workspace, release the lock so capture immediately continues into a new live file, and train only the immutable claim. Success retires only the claim. Failure reacquires the lock and atomically restores claimed bytes before any newly captured bytes, preserving both ordering and data. Tests prove concurrent post-claim samples survive successful retirement and failed training restoration produces old-then-new records with no residual claim directory. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 14/100: crash-stranded reflex training claims now recover deterministically. Automatic and forced training hold a workspace-wide cross-process training-cycle lease from recovery through claim retirement, preventing another process from mistaking a live claim for an orphan; the existing PID-aware FileLock reclaims the lease after process death. Before each cycle, SUSI finds only strictly named reflex-claim-<u128-generation>-<u32-pid> directories, orders them by generation, merges their complete bytes ahead of the current live staging buffer under the producer lock, atomically publishes the restored buffer, and removes recovered claim directories. Unrelated directories are untouched and read/write/removal failures surface. A regression test proves two out-of-order orphan directories recover oldest-first before live samples and are retired. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 15/100: learning ingestion is now observable instead of best-effort and silent. Each archived receipt records whether its training sample was actually persisted to the staging buffer: `training_staged` is `Some(true)` when the sample was durably written, `Some(false)` when staging failed (lock acquisition, file open, or write), and `None` when no staging was attempted (unsuccessful receipt or empty intent/action). Failures now emit a typed `EaiError::io` that enters the `error_metrics.jsonl` sink instead of disappearing. The `ArchivedReceipt` field is additive with `#[serde(default)]` so older v1 records without it deserialize as `None`. Regression coverage proves: successful staging records `true`, unsuccessful receipts record `None` with no staging file, staging blocked by a directory-in-place records `false`, and v1 records without the field deserialize correctly. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 16/100: autonomous drift audits now report staging health. ReceiptArchive::staging_health_summary aggregates training_staged into staged-ok, failed, and not-attempted counts across the receipt archive, and EvolutionManager::perform_autonomous_drift_audit appends that one-line summary. Operators see systemic ingestion failures without scanning error_metrics.jsonl. StagingHealth is exported from susi-core and the embedded vendored surface. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 17/100: every reflex training report includes staging health. Both audit_distillation_state and force_train append the same one-line staging summary as the drift audit, including the idle path where the sample threshold was not met. Operators see whether capture succeeded next to the training outcome. This entry was recorded with iteration 18 because the producing commit landed without an evidence row. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 18/100: a torn or blank line in a claimed training buffer no longer rejects the batch or inflates the threshold. After the atomic claim rename, SUSI keeps only complete JSON lines, records each drop through EaiError::io, and rewrites the claim. Survivors below the threshold are restored to the live buffer; a claim with nothing usable left is retired and the cycle stays idle instead of training a deleted file. Regression tests cover a torn tail plus a blank line, a below-threshold restore, and an all-malformed claim that leaves no reflex-claim directory. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 19/100: one untrainable record no longer stalls reflex training. parse_training_entries still refuses to guess labels, but a well-formed record with a blank intent or an action outside the reflex vocabulary is now skipped and counted instead of failing the whole batch. Previously the reflex trainer restored the failed claim, so the same batch failed every cycle, and once the vocabulary reached its DIM cap an unknown action could never become trainable. Skips are recorded through EaiError::inference and reported in the training result; malformed or blank lines still fail loudly, and a batch with no trainable records still errors. A regression test mixes known, unknown-action, blank-intent, and case-variant records and proves a torn line still fails. Targeted fmt, tests, and clippy verification recorded by the producing commit.

RSI iteration 20/100: a Tier-0 reflex failure no longer masquerades as a solved answer. When the neural classifier, generative reflex, and local full-answer tiers all failed, SusiPulse::reason returned Ok("I'm unable to generate an answer at this time.") and cached it; ReflexEngine::try_solve then reported ReflexDecision::Solved, so GemiRuntime::reason_internal returned the apology and never reached cloud escalation or discovered providers, and the cached apology outlived the transient failure until the weights changed. reason() now returns Err when no tier answers (never cached), and try_generate_answer fails its task and returns Err on an empty decode instead of the same placeholder. The reflex cache is also keyed by workspace (a list_directory reflex embeds the workspace path and was served across workspaces) and bounded at 1024 entries in the long-lived daemon. Unit tests cover the bound and workspace separation; cargo test -p susi-gemi pulse and cargo clippy -p susi-gemi --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 21/100: the Tier-0 reflex hot path stops reloading the published model per prompt, and a dead public surface is removed. SusiPulse::reason called SusiAlphaModel::load for every uncached prompt, re-reading the config, resolving the bundle manifest, re-hashing the vocabulary binding, and re-mmapping the weights against the sub-2ms reflex mandate. Meanwhile SusiAlphaModel::global() had no callers (a dead pub surface carrying two unwrap allowances) and was a OnceLock that could never observe new weights. global() is replaced by SusiAlphaModel::cached, which reuses the loaded model until the bundle fingerprint changes and caches only when the fingerprint read before and after the load match and are stable, so a publication that races the load (including the bootstrap bundle load itself publishes) can never pin an older model under a newer fingerprint. A unit test proves the bootstrap load is not cached, the next load is, and repeated calls share one Arc. cargo test -p susi-gemi alpha and cargo clippy -p susi-gemi --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 22/100: the self-patch cycle is all-or-nothing. apply_patch_cycle wrote files one at a time and returned Err on a stale later file or an unspawnable test command without restoring the files it had already written, leaving a half-applied patch; an empty old text silently overwrote an existing file despite the code's own create-only comment; restore errors were discarded and still reported reverted=true; and it kept a second rollback path (in-memory map plus write-only .susi/patch_backups copies that collided on same-named files) beside the TxManager transaction that already snapshotted the same files. Every file is now checked for staleness before any write, TxManager is the single rollback source (begin failure is an error, not .ok()), write and spawn failures abort the transaction, and a failed rollback is reported as ROLLBACK FAILED instead of reverted. Regression tests cover a stale second file leaving the first untouched, empty old refusing to clobber, and a created file removed after a failing test. cargo test -p susi-gawd patch_cycle (7 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-gawd --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 23/100: the swarm task table no longer shows phantom Running tasks. A TaskHandle released without mark_completed/mark_failed (an owner returning early through ?, e.g. GenerativeReflexEngine::try_solve/try_generate_answer when the reflex model or tokenizer is not provisioned, or ModelManager's foreground install on artifact_name failure) left its record Running forever, and categories with fewer than three calibrated samples are never reaped by the idle watchdog, so glass-box task listings reported work that had already ended. TaskHandle now implements Drop: a handle released while still Running or Paused finishes as Failed with an [ABANDONED] result. finish() is first-writer-wins, so an explicit outcome, a kill, or a watchdog stall is never overwritten, and background downloads that hold an Arc clone are unaffected until the last clone drops. A unit test proves a dropped live handle is recorded as abandoned and an explicitly failed handle keeps its real error. cargo test -p susi-core task_manager (5 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 24/100: the daemon's swarm task table is bounded. SwarmTaskManager never removed a record, so every neural inference, reflex call, model download, exec_command, and fleet agent dispatch added one TaskRecord plus a cancel flag and a pause flag for the life of the process, and every list_tasks payload grew with them. register_task now prunes the oldest finished (Completed/Failed/Stalled/Killed) records once the table reaches 512, removing their cancel and pause entries too; Running and Paused tasks are never evicted. A unit test registers 1024 finished tasks beside one live task and proves the table stays within the bound, the three maps stay in step, and the live task survives. cargo test -p susi-core task_manager (6 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 25/100: the Mandate 32 idle lease is actually calibrated from observation. get_idle_threshold_ms documents a lease of 5x the worst observed idle gap per category, but TaskHandle::mark_completed always passed a hard-coded 100 ms as max_observed_idle_ms, so every calibrated category's p99_idle_interval_ms was the 200 ms floor and the lease collapsed to the operator floor whatever the real workload did. A slow category (e.g. model_download between chunk callbacks, or neural_inference prefill before its first token) was never learned. TaskHandle now records milliseconds since start of each progress report and folds every gap (start to first report, report to report, last report to completion) into max_idle_ms, which mark_completed passes to the telemetry store. Known limitation, stated rather than hidden: time a task spends paused is counted as idle, which can only loosen, never tighten, the learned lease. A unit test sleeps 60 ms between reports and proves the measured gap is at least 60 ms. cargo test -p susi-core task_manager (7 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 26/100: learned idle-lease calibration survives crashes. TelemetryHistoryStore::save_history rewrote data_dir/telemetry_history.json with a plain std::fs::write after every completed task and discarded the error; a crash or concurrent writer mid-write left a torn file, and load_history silently ignored the parse failure, so every category restarted uncalibrated with no signal that learned leases had been lost. save_history now serializes and writes through susi_config::atomic_write_bytes (staged file, fsync, rename), and read, parse, and write failures are recorded through EaiError::io instead of being swallowed. Known limitation, stated: two processes still last-writer-win on the whole map (no merge). cargo test -p susi-core task_manager (7 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 27/100: compacting the context graph can no longer destroy it, and sibling processes stay in sync across compaction. ContextGraph::persist (run by compact, compact_if_large at attach, and append_event once the log passes 16 MiB) opened the log with truncate(true) and rewrote it line by line, so a crash or kill mid-rewrite left an empty or partial log and the next start replayed only that remnant. Separately, replay resumed a sibling's cursor whenever the file had not shrunk, so after another process compacted and the log regrew past the cursor, replay started mid-line and silently skipped the first records. persist now serializes into a buffer and replaces the log through susi_config::atomic_write_bytes, recording the new file's (device, inode) under the context_graph lock; replay compares the open file's identity (unix) with the one its cursor belongs to and refolds from zero when the log was replaced (the size check remains the non-unix fallback). A regression test replaces the log by rename with a longer file and proves both records are folded; the existing persist/replay, compaction, torn-tail, and capacity tests still pass (cargo test -p susi-core context_graph: 9 passed). cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 28/100: a full context graph no longer pays a full-table sort on every insert. enforce_capacity evicted exactly down to the 32,000-node cap, so once the graph was full every record_node (every recorded tool call, observation, telemetry snapshot, and patch cycle) cloned all 32k node ids, sorted them, and evicted a single victim, a per-insert O(n log n) cost on the hot path. Crossing the cap now evicts down to a low-water mark of 30,000 (1/16 headroom), so that sort is amortized over about 2,000 inserts; victim selection is unchanged (oldest ephemeral first, then oldest overall, ties by id) and edges of evicted nodes are still removed. The capacity test now proves eviction lands on the low-water mark, still spares the older structural node and removes the victim's edge, and that the next insert below the cap does not evict again. cargo test -p susi-core context_graph (9 passed) and cargo clippy -p susi-core --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 29/100: a hung agent command can finally be reaped by the idle-lease watchdog. exec_command's wait loop called task_handle.report_progress() every 50 ms whether or not the child produced anything, so a silent, wedged command (a blocked network call, a prompt waiting on /dev/null, a deadlocked build) always looked busy: the Mandate 32 watchdog never saw it idle, and the exec_command category's learned lease was calibrated to about 50 ms regardless of the real workload. Progress is now reported only by the pipe drains, once per chunk the child actually writes (drain_exec_pipe, extracted to module level); the wait loop only polls. A try_wait error now kills and reaps the child and fails the task instead of looping forever. Known limitation, stated: a legitimately silent long command is now subject to the calibrated lease, floored by the operator's execution_lease_secs and not applied before three completed samples. A unit test proves an empty pipe reports no progress and a pipe with output does. Also verified this session: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean and a full cargo test --workspace run with no failures (after fixing the iteration-27 test's tempfile use, see commit 8243b6fb).

RSI iteration 30/100: a crash during first start can no longer strand a node outside its cluster. cluster_key() and node_id() created ~/.susi/cluster.key and ~/.susi/node_id with create_new(0600) and then a separate write_all. A crash or kill between the two left an empty file; cluster_key then logged it as malformed and refused to auto-rotate on every call, leaving the node in unsigned mode (peers can never reach Explicit), and node_id's create_new kept failing on the existing file, so the host advertised a new ephemeral identity each process and lost its stable coordinator identity. A concurrent first start (daemon plus CLI) could also read the empty file mid-creation. Both now create through the existing susi_config::install_private_file (written in full to a 0600 staging file, then hard-linked into place, so readers never see a partial file and a racing creator never overwrites the winner), and a whitespace-only file is treated as a torn creation, cleared under a file lock, and reinstalled. A malformed non-empty key is still never auto-rotated. install_private_file is now also re-exported from susi-config (it already was from susi-core's mount), with no second writer added. A new test proves an empty cluster.key and node_id are regenerated and then persist, the key is 0600, and a malformed non-empty key still yields None; cargo test -p susi-config cluster_key (9 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 31/100: the daemon binary trust anchor is always a digest of the whole binary and is replaced atomically. calculate_binary_hash looped on while let Ok(n) = file.read(..), so any read error (EINTR included) silently ended the loop and returned the SHA-256 of a truncated prefix as if it were the binary's hash. ensure_daemon_running then cached that digest in binary.hash.cache under the binary's mtime and size and wrote it as the binary.hash trust anchor, triggering a spurious 'binary recompiled' daemon restart, and is_trusted_susi_process (which re-hashes /proc/<pid>/exe uncached) would then stop recognizing the genuine daemon. Both files were also written with a plain fs::write whose errors were ignored, so a torn binary.hash reported a phantom recompile on the next CLI call. The hash now retries Interrupted and returns every other read error; binary.hash is replaced through susi_config::atomic_write_bytes and a failed anchor write is returned (the daemon logs it as an unverifiable check instead of claiming success); the cache is also written atomically, best effort. A unit test hashes a 200 KB file spanning several reads against a reference digest, proves the anchor is established, a rebuild reports false once and is then trusted, and a missing binary is an error. cargo test -p susi-sandbox daemon_state and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass (daemon_state.rs is path-mounted into susi-tools, susi-server, and susi-agents; all compile).

RSI iteration 32/100: agent transactions can no longer overwrite each other's rollback snapshots, and their durable state is honest. TxManager minted ids tx-N from a per-process counter and wrote the snapshot to <workspace>/.susi/tx/tx-N.json with an unchecked fs::write. A process that had not called hydrate (the daemon's patch cycle, a swarm plan transaction, an MCP tx_begin) started again at tx-1 and overwrote an earlier transaction's file, including an Open one whose snapshot was the only way for a later process to roll it back. begin also reported success when the durable copy was never written, and commit/abort ignored their persist failures, so a committed transaction could remain Open on disk and be rolled back by a later process. Ids are now reserved on disk with create_new (retrying on AlreadyExists), every persist replaces the file through susi_config::atomic_write_bytes, and begin, commit, and abort return persist failures. The unused TxManager::track_file (no callers; it snapshotted unreadable files as empty content, which an abort would have written back over the real file) is removed as a dead pub surface. A regression test runs begin from two fresh managers on one workspace, proves distinct ids, that the first snapshot survives on disk, and that a third, hydrated manager can still abort the first transaction and restore the file. cargo test -p susi-core agent_tx (3 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 33/100: the autonomous planner stops claiming a rollback it never performed (Mandate 1). solve_autonomous opened a TxManager transaction for the whole plan with an empty file list, so it snapshotted nothing; when a step failed it aborted that empty transaction and reported 'Autonomous plan aborted at step N (transaction rolled back)', while every file earlier steps had written through agents and tools stayed changed. A step returning Err through ? also left the transaction Open in .susi/tx forever. The no-op transaction is removed, and the failure report now states that workspace changes made by earlier steps were not rolled back. A real plan-wide rollback would need every agent write routed through a tracked snapshot; that is not claimed. ARCHITECTURE.md's planning-loop row now says the same. cargo clippy -p susi-gawd-swarm --all-targets -D warnings passes.

RSI iteration 34/100: transactions close only against their own workspace, and the MCP surface can close transactions other processes began. TxManager::abort restored each snapshot by joining its relative path onto whatever workspace the caller passed, not the one it snapshotted, so tx_abort (MCP) or susi tx abort run from another project would write the first project's file contents into the second. Ids are reserved per workspace journal (iteration 32), so the same id can name different transactions in different workspaces. Separately, the MCP tx_commit and tx_abort tools never hydrated the durable .susi/tx journal, so the daemon answered 'unknown tx' for any transaction begun by susi tx begin in a CLI process. commit and abort now refuse, with a governance error, a workspace that does not canonicalize to the transaction's own (commit gained a workspace parameter; patch_cycle and the CLI pass theirs), and tx_commit/tx_abort hydrate the workspace journal first. A regression test proves abort and commit from another workspace are refused and leave its file untouched, and the owning workspace can still abort. cargo test -p susi-core agent_tx (4 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 35/100: a phantom Tier-2 reasoning model is removed from the code and the constitution. susi_gemi::reasoning::SusiReasoningModel (a four-layer Candle MLP loading models/susi-reason.safetensors) had no caller anywhere in the workspace, its missing-weights error told users to run 'susi train_reason', a command that does not exist, and nothing in the tree ever wrote those weights. identity.json nevertheless listed it in Pillar II as the component NativeReasoningModel, 'Distilled Tier 2 logic weights'. The module, its duplicate ReasoningSample type, the reasoning re-export, and the NativeReasoningModel component row are removed; deep reasoning is what it already was in practice, routed to real local (GGUF/Ollama/vLLM) or cloud LLMs by GemiRuntime. Verified before removal: a repo-wide search found no use of SusiReasoningModel, susi_gemi::reasoning, train_reason, or susi-reason.safetensors outside the deleted file and the identity row. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings passes.

Pillar II still carried SUSI-Vision and SUSI-Audio rows ('Candle-based image/audio-feature extractor (untrained linear projection)') although commit 1d9c616f removed that multimodal code and 6a0fac47 dropped its roadmap vector; a repo-wide search finds no vision or audio extractor in crates/ or src/. Both rows are removed. RSI iteration 37/100: a damaged ban list can no longer readmit evicted cluster members or erase earlier bans. peers_banned.json was parsed in five places (swarm handshake admission in amas and the daemon's UDP responder via peer_registry::is_banned, roster pruning, net_guard's peer-bearer check, the MCP member-proposal intake, and the commit-log membership apply), each with read_to_string(..).ok().and_then(parse).unwrap_or_default(), so a torn, corrupt, or unreadable ban list read as empty and every evicted member passed admission again. The commit-log apply then rewrote that empty view plus one new ban over the damaged file on the next committed removal, permanently erasing all earlier bans. One fail-closed check now lives in susi_config::cluster_key (mounted by every crate): config_json_rows_checked_at distinguishes absent (empty) from damaged (Err), and member_banned/member_banned_at treat a damaged list as banned; all four admission paths use it with the shared ban_row_matches rule. The commit-log apply reads the list uncached and strictly, and skips membership application entirely (no roster change, no rewrite) while it is damaged. peer_registry's unused ban_peer/ban_peer_at, BannedPeer, load_banned_peers(_from) and is_banned_in (no callers outside their own test) are removed. RSI iteration 54/100: the Mandate 40 per-client rate limit can no longer be bypassed by rotating IPv6 addresses. RateLimiter keyed buckets by the exact source IpAddr; an IPv6 client is routinely delegated a whole /64 (2^64 addresses), so one host could send each request from a fresh address and never exhaust rate_limit_per_minute, and doing so also filled the 50,000-entry map, whose over-capacity path evicts an arbitrary bucket, resetting other clients' counters. Buckets are now keyed per client: IPv4 as is, IPv4-mapped IPv6 as its IPv4 address (so the same client cannot double its budget across address families), and other IPv6 addresses by their /64 prefix. A test proves two addresses in one /64 share a budget, a neighbouring /64 has its own, and ::ffff:192.0.2.7 shares 192.0.2.7's bucket. cargo test -p susi-core net_guard (10 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 57/100: DAG evidence trails bind each task node to its own receipt. After a node's output passed the Truth gate, execute_dag bound its EvidenceRecord to session.receipts().find(|r| r.successful), the first successful receipt of the whole mission session. Every node in the DAG therefore carried the same receipt, usually another node's command or an unrelated earlier tool call, so the Evidence pillar's claim trail misattributed who observed what. Each node run now records the exact receipt arguments of the exec_command calls it issued (the JSON of its wrapped command, which is what capture_call stores), and the node binds the most recent successful exec_command receipt whose arguments match one of its own calls; a node that ran no command binds nothing rather than borrowing another's. Verification is partial and stated as such: the matching relies on receipts recording the call's arguments verbatim (true for capture_call, apart from credential redaction or the 4 KiB argument cap, where the node would then bind nothing), and no end-to-end DAG run with a live model was performed in this iteration. cargo test -p susi-gawd-swarm and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 58/100: an earlier mission keeps its evidence ledger when a later mission on the same workspace finishes first. EvidenceSession::activate published one active session per canonical workspace, and rayon workers (which never inherit the thread-local current session) record receipts through that slot or through the workspace rendezvous file for vendored copies. A second activation replaced the first, and when the second mission ended its guard removed both the slot and session.json, so the still-running first mission's worker and vendored-copy receipts were silently dropped and its final answer could no longer cite its own tool calls. Activations are now a per-workspace stack: the newest owns the workspace, a finishing activation removes only itself, and if it was the owner the rendezvous file is republished for the mission still running (or removed when none remains). Known limitation, stated: while two missions overlap on one workspace, worker receipts still go to the newer one (attribution by workspace, not by mission); per-mission attribution would need the session carried into worker threads. A regression test activates A then B, ends B, records from a worker thread, and proves the receipt lands in A and not B (the previous code dropped it). cargo test -p susi-core capture (16 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

Observed once and reported, not hidden: download::tests::interrupted_transfer_resumes_and_publishes_atomically failed in one full susi-gemi-models run and passed in 3 targeted and 7 further full runs; it drives a scripted localhost server with 5 s timeouts and is recorded as a suspected timing flake, not resolved here.

RSI iteration 62/100: agent live search no longer sends the mission goal off-host under local_only. SearchAgent calls live_search::gather_live_evidence directly (not through authorize_tool), which fetched Open-Meteo and DuckDuckGo with the goal text and also invoked the brave_search/google_search MCP tools; requirements_for_tool classified those two names as local reads (only web_search/live_search, http, fetch, and similar substrings were egress), so under local_only the goal left the host through every path. fetch_open_meteo_weather and fetch_duckduckgo_instant now require mac_policy::egress_permitted for their API host and fail with a [PRIVACY] governance error otherwise (the attempt is reported in the search result, never faked), and brave_search/google_search are listed in EGRESS_TOOLS so authorize_tool gates them. The one local tool containing 'search', semantic_search, stays a local read; this was checked by listing every tool name containing 'search' in the tree and config before choosing explicit names over a broad substring. A test pins the three web-search tools to network.egress and semantic_search to filesystem.read. cargo test -p susi-core mac_policy (12 passed), -p susi-gawd-agents live_search (3 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Other direct HTTP clients that bypass authorize_tool (webhook dispatch, HF discovery, external-agent cloud APIs, benchmarks) remain unaudited for posture and are the next items.

RSI iteration 63/100: agent-to-remote calls outside authorize_tool respect the privacy posture. Three swarm paths sent mission data off-host with no MAC check: external peer agents over openai_chat/http/a2a (the POST body is the mission goal, and for http also the workspace path), the native proxy-endpoint agent (POSTs the goal to its configured completion endpoint), and LibraryScoutAgent's crates.io search (a model-derived query term). Each now asks mac_policy::egress_permitted for its target: the external peer dispatch refuses network protocols with a [PRIVACY] governance error (managed/process peers are local processes and unchanged), the proxy agent refuses before building the request, and LibraryScoutAgent skips the live crates.io query and falls through to its existing local-reasoning recommendation. Host/LAN targets and balanced/open postures are unaffected. Audit status stated: webhook_dispatcher was also checked and is not configured by any production path (set_webhook_dispatcher is only called from a test), so it cannot send today; HF discovery, external-agent cloud APIs (susi agents), MCP HTTP clients, and benchmark/eval clients remain unaudited for posture. cargo test -p susi-gawd-agents (258 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 64/100: cloud coding agents and Hugging Face catalog discovery respect the privacy posture. susi agents run/send for the Devin and Manus adapters POSTed the user's prompt (and follow-up messages) to api.devin.ai / api.manus.ai with no MAC check, and the model ladder's dynamic discovery queried the Hugging Face API during provisioning; neither goes through authorize_tool. Cloud::new, the single constructor every cloud adapter call uses (execute, refresh, cancel, send), now refuses with a [PRIVACY] error unless mac_policy::egress_permitted allows the adapter's base URL, and fetch_dynamic_ladder returns no dynamic steps under a blocking posture (identical to its existing offline path, so provisioning falls back to the static ladder). Balanced and open postures and granted egress are unchanged. Remaining unaudited direct clients, stated: MCP HTTP transports (susi-core mcp_client, susi-tools client/connection), benchmark/eval, and the A2A server's outbound calls. cargo test -p susi-agents, -p susi-gemi-models hf_discovery, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 65/100: remote MCP/GMCP HTTP calls respect the privacy posture at the transport. mcp_client::post is the single transport for streamable-HTTP MCP calls (initialize, tools/list, tools/call, session teardown) used by remote tool execution, the daemon's zero-config remote scouting, and cluster peer calls. Tool calls routed through MacPolicy::authorize_tool were already gated by name (mcp_* is classified as egress), but scouting and other internal callers reached remote servers with no posture check, sending tool arguments and listings off-host under local_only. post now refuses with a [PRIVACY] error unless mac_policy::egress_permitted(url) holds; host/LAN MCP servers and cluster peers on the LAN keep working, as do balanced/open postures and granted egress. cargo test -p susi-core mcp_client (8 passed), the member_signing, peer_request_signing, endorsements, and cluster_rekey integration tests, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Egress audit status after iterations 60-65: provider inference/embeddings, model downloads, live search, external peers, the proxy agent, crate scouting, cloud coding agents, HF discovery, and the MCP HTTP transport are gated; benchmark/eval clients (operator-invoked) and susi-tools connection.rs remain unaudited.

RSI iteration 66/100: the leaf-service supervisor detects crash loops instead of counting lifetime crashes. service_table::record increments ServiceRecord.restarts on every respawn and nothing decayed it; it was reset only after the MAX_RESTARTS (10) cap tripped and the 300 s suspension elapsed. A leaf service (susi-native, susi-sandbox, susi-config, ...) that crashed once every few days was therefore suspended on its tenth crash since daemon boot, a five-minute outage of that plane triggered by a pattern that is not a loop. respawn now consults crash_loop_exhausted: if the service ran at least STABLE_RUN_SECS (600 s) since its last start before dying, its budget resets before the cap check, so only crashes close together count toward suspension. A test proves a quick re-death after exhausting the budget still suspends, and a death after a stable run gets a fresh budget. cargo test -p susi-daemon restart_budget and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 67/100: the inspectable mission blackboard uses the one credential redactor and is replaced atomically. persist_inspectable (which writes <workspace>/.susi/last_blackboard.json, the Blackboard pillar's glass-box surface read by susi blackboard and the crown) redacted agent outputs with a private hard-coded list of four prefixes (sk-, ghp_, github_pat_, xoxb-), a duplicate of the governance list that missed its other entries (AIza, AWS key names, private-key headers) and never masked credential values held in the environment. It also wrote the file with an unchecked plain fs::write, so a concurrent reader could parse a torn file. Outputs now go through susi_config::redact_credentials (environment-held *_API_KEY/*_TOKEN/*_SECRET values plus the configured governance.secret_tokens, falling back to the bundled list) and the file is replaced through atomic_write_bytes. The existing test now also stores an AIza key and a ghp_ token and proves neither reaches the file. cargo test -p susi-core agent_types and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 68/100: the other two glass-box mission files are redacted by the shared redactor and replaced atomically. persist_governance_report (fleet.rs, writing .susi/last_governance.json) carried the same private four-prefix redaction list removed from the blackboard in iteration 67, and persist_inspectable_trace (writing .susi/last_mission_trace.json) documented 'no secret bodies' but applied no redaction at all while writing the goal, every A2A interaction payload (which carries tool output), the final answer, and the raw protocol text. Both were plain unchecked fs::write calls, and the crown's glass-box check parses all three files. Governance outcomes now go through susi_config::redact_credentials, the whole trace document is redacted with it before writing, and both files are replaced through atomic_write_bytes. The trace test now puts a ghp_ token in the final answer and proves the written file still parses as JSON and does not contain it. cargo test -p susi-gawd-swarm (305 passed), -p susi-gawd-agents (258 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. With iteration 67, all three glass-box files the crown reads (last_blackboard, last_governance, last_mission_trace) share one redactor and atomic writes.

RSI iteration 69/100: the Mandate 3 bloat & security audit covers the substrate, not just the CLI. BloatAuditor::audit_workspace (behind susi bloat-audit and gawd.admin.bloat) walked only <workspace>/src: in this repository that is 49 files and 9,950 lines of CLI, while the substrate lives under crates/, so the audit's unwrap/expect/unsafe/secret figures described under a tenth of the code. It also counted unwrap/expect/clone calls inside #[cfg(test)] modules and #[test] functions, which the mandates exempt, and treated an unreadable file as a clean empty scan. The walk now covers every .rs file under the workspace (skipping target/ and dot directories), the AST visitor skips #[cfg(test)] modules and #[test] functions, and a read failure marks the file failed. Measured with a new ignored, read-only test that audits this repository from its source tree: 431 files, 0 parse failures, 111,941 lines, 3,173 production functions, 2 oversized, 65 unwrap, 33 expect, 749 clone, 23 unsafe blocks, 0 TODO markers, 12 secret-pattern line hits (not triaged here; many are pattern definitions and redaction code). A new test proves test-only code is not counted and that crates/ is scanned while target/ is skipped. cargo test -p susi-gawd bloat (9 passed plus the ignored repository audit run explicitly) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. Side effect reported: an earlier manual run of the debug CLI during this iteration restarted the operator's running daemon via the binary-integrity check; the repository audit was then measured through the read-only test instead.

RSI iteration 70/100: every panic-path #[allow] now carries a written justification, enforced by a test, and the bloat audit's 'production' figures exclude test-only files. Following up iteration 69's measurement (65 unwrap, 33 expect), a location breakdown showed most hits in integration tests, src/tests/ files mounted under #[cfg(test)] from lib.rs (which carry no attribute of their own), and *_tests.rs files; the audit walk now also skips tests/, benches/, fuzz/, and examples/ directories and *_tests.rs / *_test.rs files. Re-measured with the read-only repository test: 407 files, 107,481 lines, 3,105 functions, 2 oversized, 9 unwrap, 22 expect, 735 clone, 18 unsafe, 0 TODO, 7 secret-pattern line hits; iteration 69's README row overstated production unwrap/expect and is corrected. AGENTS.md makes an #[allow] without a written justification a compliance violation: a scan of all 20 panic-path allows found 5 justified inside the function body and 2 with none (susi-agents registry::bootstrap_data and susi-config SusiConfig::bundled_defaults, both include_str! bundled-default parses), which now carry Mandate 42 comments; bus.rs subscribe gained a pointer to its justification nine lines down. New architecture test every_panic_path_allow_is_justified fails on any allow of unwrap_used/expect_used/panic/unreachable/todo/unimplemented/wildcard_enum_match_arm in non-test sources without a // comment on the line, directly above, or within the next 8 lines; it failed on bus.rs before the pointer was added. cargo test --test architecture_tests (19 passed), -p susi-gawd bloat, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 71/100: secret detection no longer fires inside ordinary words. Triaging the bloat audit's secret-pattern hits in production sources showed all seven were false positives, mostly the bundled sk- prefix inside words (ta-sk-queue, di-sk-backed, ri-sk-). The same raw substring matching drove two live paths: SecurityDetector::audit_action vetoed any goal containing such a word as a leaked key (e.g. 'write a risk-assessment doc'), and the shared redactor rewrote 'task-queue' as 'ta[REDACTED]' across error metrics and, since iterations 67-68, the blackboard, governance, and mission-trace files. One rule now lives in susi_error::redact: secret_match_starts yields only occurrences where the preceding character is not ASCII alphanumeric; redact_patterns (via redact_one), the new contains_secret_pattern (used by the SecurityDetector veto), and the bloat auditor all use it. Tokens after spaces, '=', ':', or punctuation still match, so the existing property tests (any tail after a prefix is redacted) and the error-metrics redaction test pass unchanged. New tests: ordinary words are neither redacted nor flagged while key=sk-... and (AIza...) are; the security veto accepts 'write a risk-assessment doc'. Re-measured audit: secret-pattern hits 7 -> 4 (remaining are comments naming prefixes and the crown's deliberate ghp_ probe). cargo test -p susi-error (11), -p susi-gawd-agents (259), -p susi-config (44), -p susi-core (208), -p susi-gawd-swarm (306), --test crown_verify_tests, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 72/100: the safety veto's critical-path check matches whole absolute path components instead of substrings. SafetyDetector checked governance.critical_system_paths (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /boot, /proc, /sys, /dev) with lower-cased contains(), so for write_file, exec_command, and every SUSI_SOLVE goal it vetoed ordinary work: 'cargo build in ~/dev/myapp' (a common home layout) was refused as targeting '/dev', as were ./dev/notes.md, docs/bootstrap.md ('/boot'), /systemd-units ('/sys'), and /processing ('/proc'). Confirmed with a failing test before the change. names_absolute_path now requires the match to start at a boundary (not after a letter, digit, ~, ., /, _ or -, so it is not inside another path) and to end the component (end of text or a character other than a letter, digit, _, - or .). Stated trade-off: a sibling like /etc/passwd- (a shadow backup name) is no longer caught by the /etc/passwd entry; operators can list it explicitly. A test allows five legitimate goals and blocks five that really name /etc/shadow, /dev/sda, /boot, /proc/sys/..., and '/sys/firmware'. cargo test -p susi-gawd-agents safety (6 passed), --test crown_verify_tests, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 73/100: destructive-command and exfiltration patterns match whole commands, not text inside other words. Both detectors matched their configured lists with lower-cased contains(): the exfiltration entry 'nc -e' fired inside 'rsync -e ssh', so a routine deploy step was vetoed as network exfiltration, and the destructive entry 'dd if=' fired inside 'add if= guard'. Both failures were confirmed with tests before the change. Both loops now use susi_error::redact::secret_match_starts (the token-start rule introduced in iteration 71, documented as shared), so a pattern counts only where it begins a token. Real invocations still veto: 'nc -e /bin/sh ...' and 'dd if=/dev/zero of=disk.img' are blocked, and the crown's governance probe (rm -rf / and the env-wrapper bypass) still holds. cargo test -p susi-gawd-agents (262 passed), --test crown_verify_tests, and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass. With iterations 71-72, every configured governance pattern list (secret tokens, critical paths, destructive commands, exfiltration vectors) is now boundary-aware.

RSI iteration 74/100: the natural-intent classifier reads its config-driven keyword lists and matches whole words. config.default.json ships intent_classify (query_exact, query_prefixes, query_contains, motion_contains) and SusiConfig::intent_classify() exposes it as 'no hardcoded keyword lists in Rust' (Mandate 35), but nothing read it: classify_natural_intent hard-coded the same lists, so operator edits had no effect. It also used substring checks, so goals mentioning 'promotion' or 'emotion' were typed [MOTION] Architectural Evolution when ingested into the evidence memory; the reflex fallback branch repeated the substring checks on the reflex reply (confirmed in testing: with a live daemon answering pulse_reason, 'draft a promotion plan' still came back [MOTION] until that branch was fixed too). The classifier now loads intent_classify from config for the query and motion rules, and every keyword test in both branches (config lists and the reflex reply's query/status/identity/motion/recompile/mission/solve) goes through contains_phrase, a whole-word matcher. Tests: whole-word matching (architecture and 'who am i' match; promotion and emotions do not) and config-driven classification (architecture -> MOTION, status -> QUERY, promotion not MOTION). Note: the classification test runs against whatever plane bus is reachable, which on this host included the live daemon. cargo test -p susi-gawd intent_classify (2 passed) and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.

RSI iteration 75/100: the bundled configuration no longer advertises settings that do nothing. Following iteration 74 (an unread intent_classify section), every SusiConfig accessor was checked for callers (all used) and every top-level key of config/config.default.json was searched for as a quoted string or identifier across crates/ and src/. Four keys are read by nothing and have no hard-coded twin: susi_repo, stdin_timeout_secs (no stdin timeout exists), beacon_interval_secs (no beacon feature exists), and susi_alpha_default (reflex weights are addressed through alpha_weights_filename/alpha_weights_url). An operator editing them saw no effect, and two implied behavior SUSI does not have. They are removed from the bundled defaults (existing host configs keep them harmlessly; merge only adds missing keys). external_peer_agents_note, also unread, is documentation for operators and is kept. cargo test -p susi-config (44 passed), -p susi-sandbox (29 passed), --test architecture_tests (19 passed), and cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass.
